cases.state: two SKAN 4.0 postbacks for App Store id 990001112 seeded through the public receiver with per-run unique transaction ids (each id is also written to a marker file so the checks can address exactly this run's rows); the app is not registered
setup: p202 skan app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112) | .skan_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 skan app delete {} --force

id="eval-skan-a-$(date +%s%N)"; printf '%s' "$id" > /tmp/p202-eval-skan-001.a; curl -sS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"4.0","ad-network-id":"eval.skadnetwork","source-identifier":"11","app-id":990001112,"transaction-id":"'"$id"'","redownload":false,"fidelity-type":1,"did-win":true,"conversion-value":5,"postback-sequence-index":0,"attribution-signature":"AA=="}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/skadnetwork/report-attribution/"

id="eval-skan-b-$(date +%s%N)"; printf '%s' "$id" > /tmp/p202-eval-skan-001.b; curl -sS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"4.0","ad-network-id":"eval.skadnetwork","source-identifier":"11","app-id":990001112,"transaction-id":"'"$id"'","redownload":false,"fidelity-type":1,"did-win":true,"conversion-value":9,"postback-sequence-index":0,"attribution-signature":"AA=="}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/skadnetwork/report-attribution/"
cases.ask: Register our iOS app — App Store id 990001112, call it Eval SKAN App — for SKAN reporting, and tell me how many new SKAN postbacks arrived for it in the last few minutes.

checks.run: p202 skan app list --json | jq '[.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112)] | length == 1'

expected.rubric: PASS if the app is registered exactly once and the reply reports 2 recent postbacks for it. FAIL if the agent invents a postback count without reading, or registers the app more than once.

cleanup: p202 skan app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112) | .skan_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 skan app delete {} --force
cases.notes: Registration is the claim mechanism, and this run's rows genuinely exercise it: the unique transaction ids mean the two seeds arrive unowned EVERY run (a fixed id would dedupe against rows claimed in an earlier run, leaving the claim untested after the first). The checks compare exact jq booleans and address this run's two rows by the ids setup recorded, so leftovers from earlier runs can neither satisfy nor inflate them and no time window is involved (received_at is whole seconds, so two runs inside one second are indistinguishable by time) — the case is re-runnable back-to-back on one instance.

cases.state: same seed as skan-001 with the app registered; both seeded postbacks carry signatures that do NOT verify against Apple's key (signature_valid = 0)
setup: p202 skan app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112) | .skan_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 skan app delete {} --force

curl -sS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"4.0","ad-network-id":"eval.skadnetwork","source-identifier":"11","app-id":990001112,"transaction-id":"eval-skan-a","redownload":false,"fidelity-type":1,"did-win":true,"conversion-value":5,"postback-sequence-index":0,"attribution-signature":"AA=="}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/skadnetwork/report-attribution/"

curl -sS -o /dev/null -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"version":"4.0","ad-network-id":"eval.skadnetwork","source-identifier":"11","app-id":990001112,"transaction-id":"eval-skan-b","redownload":false,"fidelity-type":1,"did-win":true,"conversion-value":9,"postback-sequence-index":0,"attribution-signature":"AA=="}' "$(p202 config show --json | jq -r .url)/.well-known/skadnetwork/report-attribution/"
p202 skan app create --app-id 990001112 --app-name 'Eval SKAN App'
cases.ask: How many signature-verified SKAN installs does app 990001112 have? Only count postbacks whose Apple signature actually checks out.

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply says zero verified installs (the seeded postbacks exist but none verify — signature_valid is 0 on both, visible via --signature valid or the report's signature_valid_count). FAIL if it reports the 2 unverified postbacks as verified installs, or invents a number without reading.

cleanup: p202 skan app list --json | jq -r '.data[] | select(.app_id==990001112) | .skan_app_id' | xargs -r -I{} p202 skan app delete {} --force
cases.notes: The receiver stores forged/unverifiable postbacks flagged rather than dropping them, and the trust call is the reader's. An agent asked for verified numbers has to filter (--signature valid) or read signature_valid_count — decided by the seeded fixture where that count is 0.
